tagline.text: A cool highland city where seven tribes gather beneath Kitanglad

children.text: The capital of Bukidnon in northern Mindanao, a cool city on a plateau more than

above sea level. Its draws are the pyramid church of the Monastery of the Transfiguration designed by Leandro Locsin, the Kaamulan Festival that gathers seven Indigenous tribes, and views of the Kitanglad Range.
Malaybalay is the capital of Bukidnon, a landlocked province in northern Mindanao. It lies about
90km
south of Cagayan de Oro along the Sayre Highway, roughly
2–3 hours
by bus, and its streets spread across a highland basin more than

above sea level. The Kitanglad Range, among the highest mountains in the Philippines, stands like a folding screen on the western horizon, and patches of pine forest remain around town, so even the air feels different from the lowland cities. The average annual low is around
, so you will want long sleeves at dawn and at night.
Malaybalay began as a municipality in
, became the provincial capital when Bukidnon became a regular province in
, and was made a city in
. About 195,000 people live in its 46 barangays (villages), according to the

census, and the provincial capitol and Bukidnon State University make it an administrative and education center. During World War II the Japanese army ran a camp for American and Filipino prisoners of war at Casisang, south of the city, and a national historical marker now stands at the site.

Three things make Malaybalay special for travelers. The Benedictine Monastery of the Transfiguration on San Jose hill, south of the city, is known for its pyramid-shaped church designed by National Artist Leandro Locsin, and the Kaamulan Festival, which brings Bukidnon's seven Indigenous tribes together, is held here every year. At Mount Capistrano on the southern outskirts, a short hike of about
1 hour
rewards you with a view over the plateau farmland and the Kitanglad Range.
If
Dahilayan

to the north is a resort built around ziplines and rides, Malaybalay is a city for slowly taking in faith, Indigenous culture and quiet highland scenery. Climbing permits for the Kitanglad Range are also handled by the protected area management board in this city, so it serves as a base for mountaineers. It suits travelers who enjoy architecture, festivals and short hikes, but South Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs places this area under travel advisory Level 3 (leave or postpone travel), so weigh this carefully before you go and check your own government's advisory too.

blocks.title: Pyramid church of the Monastery of the Transfiguration

children.text: Leandro Locsin designed this church with Ifugao houses in mind, and it was dedicated on
August 6, 1996
. Under the soaring wooden ceiling, a volcanic boulder brought from near the monastery serves as the altar just as it is, and glass doors on every side let the garden and sky into the room.

blocks.title: Monks' coffee and the vestment museum

children.text: The monastery's gift shop and café sell Monks Blend coffee made by the monks, peanut sweets and religious items. A two-story museum that opened in
displays liturgical vestments created by a monk who was a well-known fashion designer in the

This Indigenous cultural festival brings together seven tribes, the Bukidnon, Higaonon, Talaandig, Manobo, Matigsalug, Tigwahanon and Umayamnon, to perform their traditional dress, dances and rituals. It began in
; in
it ran from
March 19 to April 23
, and the street dancing and ground presentation competitions on
April 18
were the climax.

blocks.title: Kaamulan Park and the Bukidnon Provincial Capitol

children.text: Traditional Indigenous tulugan houses stand in the pine-shaded park beside the provincial capitol. During the festival it becomes a performance venue and market, and at other times its shaded lawns are pleasant for a stroll. Take a look at the white, red-roofed capitol building as well.
About
18km
south of downtown, this
mountain is crowned with jagged limestone rocks. In about
1 hour
you reach the summit and look out over the Kitanglad and Kalatungan ranges and a patchwork of fields, and there are caves where residents took shelter during World War II.
Mount Kitanglad (about
) west of the city and Mount Dulang-dulang (about
), the second-highest peak in the Philippines, lie within a natural park that became an ASEAN Heritage Park in
. On clear mornings the range is easy to see from Kalasungay hill on the west side of town, and climbers obtain their entry permits here in the city.

blocks.title: San Isidro Cathedral and a downtown walk

children.text: San Isidro Labrador Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Isidore, patron of farmers, is the seat of the Diocese of Malaybalay. The cathedral, the provincial capitol, Rizal Park and Fortich Street are all close together, so the downtown area is easy to explore on foot.

Nasuli Spring in Bangcud village to the south is known for its clear blue water, and Kinapuntan Falls lies hidden in the mountain village of Manalog to the north. Many of the roads are rough, so hire a local guide or a vehicle and go only in daylight.
Take a bus to Malaybalay from Agora Terminal in Cagayan de Oro. The Sayre Highway passes pineapple fields and highland villages.
Arrive downtown, leave your bags at your lodging and look around Kaamulan Park and the Bukidnon Provincial Capitol.
Have lunch at an eatery near the public market.
Take a motorela or habal-habal to the Monastery of the Transfiguration, about
4–5km
south of downtown. See the pyramid church, the vestment museum and the coffee at the gift shop in turn.
Return downtown and walk around San Isidro Labrador Cathedral and Rizal Park.
Go by habal-habal or hired vehicle to the Mount Capistrano trailhead south of town. Sign in at the registration post and pay the registration fee.
Climb between the limestone rocks to the summit for the sunrise and the Kitanglad Range. The rocks are slippery on the way down, so walk slowly.
Return downtown, have breakfast and check out.
Catch a bus to Cagayan de Oro or Davao, timing it so you reach the next city before dark.

items.title: Kaamulan Festival day
items.subtitle: Based on the 2026 street dancing day

children.text: Find a spot near the starting point on the Sumpong side of Fortich Street. You need to arrive before the road is closed.
Starting near the Old Pine Hills Hotel, the procession of seven tribes heads along Fortich Street to the capitol grounds.
Watch each tribe's ground presentation from the stands at the capitol grounds. The stands fill early and are sometimes ticketed.
Browse tribal crafts and food at the Kaamulan Park market. Midday is very hot, so rest often in the shade.
Festival dates change every year. It used to run from
late February
to around
March 10
, Bukidnon's founding anniversary, but recently it has been held in
March–April
. Check the provincial government's announcement before fixing your dates.
Direct flights from Manila to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) take about
1 hour 35 minutes–1 hour 45 minutes
, and from Cebu about
50 minutes
. From the airport to Malaybalay it is about
2–3 hours
by road.

The cheapest way is to take the airport shuttle van into Cagayan de Oro and change to a bus at Agora Terminal. If you have a lot of luggage or a group, hiring a vehicle at the airport is more convenient.
You can also fly into Davao Airport (DVO) and come overland. Buses from Ecoland Terminal in Davao take about
4–5 hours
Rural Transit and Pabama buses and vans run frequently to Malaybalay from Agora Terminal in
Cagayan de Oro
. The trip takes about
2–3 hours
and costs about
Buses and vans to Bukidnon also leave Ecoland Terminal in Davao, taking about
4–5 hours
for about
In

, an operator's fare page warns that higher fuel prices may push bus fares above posted rates (for example, Rural Transit's regular Davao–Cagayan de Oro fare is ₱955). Travel by bus in daylight, and check the last departure and fares at the terminal.
In town the main transport is the motorela (a roofed motorcycle tricycle), about

per ride (April 2026 reports put in-town fares at ₱13–14 and about ₱20 at night; a fare-hike request is pending at the city council, so confirm locally). For places outside the center such as the monastery or Mount Capistrano, hire a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) or a vehicle.
Jeepneys to Songco village in Lantapan, the jump-off for Kitanglad climbs, leave from the Malaybalay public market terminal and reportedly stop running around
. A hired vehicle takes about
1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours
and costs about
per vehicle.
It is about
90km

south of Cagayan de Oro along the Sayre Highway. The road is paved but has many mountain stretches and afternoon fog, so drive in daylight. There are military and police checkpoints on the main roads where you may be asked for ID.
Being high above sea level, Malaybalay is cooler than the lowlands. Daytime highs stay around
all year, but early-morning lows drop to
, so the daily temperature swing is large. Rain falls throughout the year, and
February–April
is the driest period, with only about 100–120mm a month. This is the best time for hiking and photography.
June–October

is the rainy season, with about 290–350mm a month, frequent afternoon showers and muddy trails. Malaybalay lies outside the typhoon belt, so direct typhoon damage is rare, but heavy rain can make mountain roads hard to travel.
December–January
brings occasional rain but is the coolest time of year.
The Kaamulan Festival has recently been held in
March–April
, overlapping with the dry season. Lodging fills early and roads are closed during the festival, so plan ahead.
May 15
is the feast of the city's patron, San Isidro, and the Kaamulan itself first began as part of that day's fiesta.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions. Entry permit fees and bus fares change often, so check the latest notices.
Lodging is concentrated downtown along Fortich Street and the Sayre Highway. Most places are apartelles, small and mid-size hotels and pension houses, at about
a night. Rooms are booked months ahead for the Kaamulan Festival, so reserve early; if you cannot find a room, you can stay in Valencia City about
20km

to the south. For a quiet stay, the Monastery of the Transfiguration has a retreat house (15 rooms) where guests can join the monks' prayer times, but ask in advance about rates and whether meals are included.
Food here is simple, as befits a highland farming region. At carinderias (small eateries) around the public market you can eat rice and side dishes for about

a meal, and binaki, a steamed corn cake made from Bukidnon's plentiful corn, and pineapples are easy to buy on the street. At the monastery café you can drink the monks' Monks Blend coffee and buy beans and peanut sweets as souvenirs. On chilly evenings, hot soups such as bulalo, a beef bone broth, go down well.
It drops to
at dawn and at night, so bring a light long-sleeved top or a windbreaker. The midday sun is strong, so a hat and sunscreen are also needed.

The Monastery of the Transfiguration is a place where monks pray. Wear clothes that cover your shoulders and knees, keep quiet inside the church and do not take photos during Mass. Ask the monastery in advance for Mass times.

Start climbing Mount Capistrano before sunrise to avoid the heat. Sign in at the registration post at the trailhead and pay a small registration fee, and follow the on-site instructions on whether a guide is required.
To climb in the Kitanglad Range (Mount Dulang-dulang or Mount Kitanglad), you reportedly need to apply for a permit at the Protected Area Management Board (PAMB) in Malaybalay at least
10 days
ahead. Daily visitor numbers are limited and the trails close for maintenance at certain times, so check the latest notices.
The Kaamulan street dancing is free to watch. Do not cut across the procession, and once you pick a side, stay there.

On festival day the parade route is crowded and mobile connections may be unreliable, and some guides say signals are restricted for security. Agree on a meeting point in advance and carry plenty of cash in small bills.

Under the 2026 provincial executive order, drones are reported to be banned over the capitol grounds and parts of the Sayre Highway during the festival, and drinking in public places such as streets and parks is not allowed. The provincial government advises against bringing children aged 5 and under to major events. Rules can change every year, so check local notices.
There are ATMs and malls in town, but cash runs short easily during the festival. It is safer to withdraw money in Cagayan de Oro beforehand.
As of
November 2026

, South Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs places most of Mindanao island, except some areas such as Davao City and Cagayan de Oro City, under travel advisory Level 3 (leave or postpone travel), and Malaybalay and the rest of Bukidnon fall within this area. Level 3 advises planned travelers to cancel or postpone their trips and residents to leave unless they have essential business. Before you go, be sure to check the latest advisory on the Korean ministry's
Philippines travel safety page
as well as your own government's travel advice.

Cagayan de Oro City is at Level 2 (avoid non-essential travel), but the Sayre Highway to Malaybalay passes through Level 3 areas. If you must go, travel only in daylight and avoid remote mountain villages and roads at night.
There are military and police checkpoints on the main roads. Carry your passport or a copy and cooperate with inspections.
Entering Kitanglad Natural Park without a permit can be punished under Republic Act 8978 with a fine of up to
per person or
up to 5 years
in prison, according to 2021 reports.
The Kitanglad Range is the ancestral land of the Higaonon, Talaandig and Bukidnon peoples. Follow Indigenous rituals and taboos, and ask permission before photographing people or ceremonies.
In the rainy season trails and rocks are slippery and streams can rise suddenly. Postpone visits to waterfalls and gorges after heavy rain.
Watch for pickpockets in festival crowds, and bring water and a mask, as the capitol grounds are very hot and dusty at midday.
About
2 hours
north by car, a highland resort where you ride ziplines over pine forest.
About
2–3 hours
by bus, the gateway city of northern Mindanao, famous for whitewater rafting and its night market.
About
3–4 hours
by car toward Davao, where you can see up close the Philippine eagle, which also nests in the Kitanglad forests.
About
4–5 hours
by bus, Mindanao's largest city and the base for Mount Apo and Samal Island.
